scope: payload.items on tag_set and the simple single-object kinds: scripts/qualify_change_batch.py on a Debug build of 53d2a8fc, 61/61 steps in one owned scratch CPU 1511-1 PN. Batches of tag_create, constant_create, constant_set, constant_delete, tag_delete, tag_table_create, tag_table_rename, block_rename, block_attributes_set and type_rename each apply under one recovery archive, one baseline compile, one mutation stage, one compile and one save, list every item in order in preview.items, record a readback stage and read back with exactly the intended names. A tag_set batch renames two tags that a compiled SCL block uses; the block names the new tags afterwards and stays consistent. Six refused preparations (one object in two items, one name from two items, a name that exists, an unknown object in a later item, items on block_delete, fields beside items) name their item and leave the PLC software unchanged. Inside a software unit, with scopePath beside items, tag_create, tag_set, constant_create and tag_delete batches apply and an item naming another scope refuses with ScopeMismatch. Midway failure: TIA accepts a double quote in tag-table and tag names (those two candidate batches apply) and rejects it in a data type name, so a type_rename batch fails natively at its second item after the first was renamed; the error names items[1] and says item 0 was written, the stages hold batch_items_preflighted and no mutation_applied, the change is recovery_required with a recovery archive, another change_prepare is refused with RecoveryRequired, and change_restore retrieves the checkpoint with the PLC software equal to the state before the batch.
limitations: One owned scratch standard CPU: PLC-root scope and one software unit (tag kinds only); namespaces are not exercised.

The batch that fails after its first write is a type_rename; a block_rename batch that fails midway leaves the renamed block inconsistent, and change_restore then refuses with ScopedRecoveryRequired by the existing inconsistent-block rule (observed in an earlier run of the day, not part of this report).

The safety-tag refusal of a batch needs a project with a safety tag; the F-I/O address refusal of a tag_set and a tag_create batch was observed on an F-CPU in a run of qualify_fio_tag_routes.py that did not complete (it stopped later at vci_workspace_create on the project language) and is not curated.
Each batch has two or three items; the 100-item bound is covered by managed tests only.
Engineering only; runtime behavior is not observed.
